content.text:
**What I decided:** I won't do anything yet. The page puts **"פסגות"** with **"ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)"** at the top as leaving the most, **86,492 ₪**, so if I had to pick, that's it. But I'm not sure, and I'll ask you first. What decided it is the big number at the top, and the sentence that says the most expensive place leaves **"22,985 ₪ פחות"** on the same fund. I've heard of Psagot. I've never heard of "ילין לפידות", and I don't know if my own bank is even on the list.

**What I looked at, in order:**
- **Top of the page:** "הפקדתם 70,000 ₪", which is 10,000 now and 500 a month for 120 months. Next to it, "הכי הרבה נשאר בזוג הזה" with 86,492 ₪, "בעוד 10 שנים, אחרי דמי ניהול ומס".
- **The lines with marks on them:** I didn't try to read them. I read the one sentence under them instead.
- **Right box, "פסגות ניירות ערך בע"מ":** I read "מה החשבון גובה ב־10 שנים: 1,057 ₪". So Psagot also takes money, just less.
- **Left box:** "דמי ניהול 0% … 0.02% נאמן". I don't know what נאמן is, but 0% sounded good.
- **Lower down:** the lists of funds and accounts with red minus numbers ("‎−43 ₪", "‎−213 ₪") made me back away from those. Under Psagot I saw "דמי משמרת 699 ₪" and didn't know what it was. I stopped around there.

**Words I didn't understand:** S&P 500, (4D), קרן מחקה, iShares … UCITS ETF, צוברת, מנוטרל מט"ח, דמי משמרת, נאמן, עמלה מתמשכת. I also didn't know what the little coloured tags mean ("קרן סל", "מחזיקה את המניות", "עסקת החלפה").

**What bothered me:** The black background with grey letters. A lot of the small writing I couldn't read even with my glasses: the tags, the lines under the account names, the explanation paragraph. Also too many numbers and colours on one screen. I got tired and worried by the middle of this one screen.

input.answer: If I had to choose, it would be Psagot with the Yalin Lapidot S&P 500 fund, because the page says it leaves the most (86,492 ₪ from 70,000 ₪). But I'm not acting on it until I ask my son, because I don't know Yalin Lapidot and didn't see my bank.
